title: Krishna in the best of everything
hook: Arjuna asks where to look for Krishna, and the answer runs from the ocean to the first letter, a
carry: vibhuti: god shines in the best of everything
tomorrow: how did a robber become a saint by saying a name backwards?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last of the mudras: Savata the gardener, and your own work, offered, as worship. Today the hands rest, the mouth begins, and the first sound comes from Krishna himself.

In the middle of the Gita, on the battlefield, Arjuna has just heard that his friend and charioteer is the source of everything. So he asks what anyone would ask next. How do I keep you in mind? In what things should I think of you? Tell me again, he says. I never get tired of hearing it.
screen: `YOU ARE THE SOURCE OF EVERYTHING.` → `WHERE DO I LOOK FOR YOU?` → `TELL ME AGAIN.`

segments.voice: Krishna answers with a list, one of the loveliest in the Gita. Among waters, I am the ocean. Among things that stand firm, the Himalaya. Among trees, the sacred fig. Among rivers, the Ganga. And then, in paraphrase: among letters, I am the letter a. Then he gives the key to the whole list: whatever is glorious, beautiful or mighty, know that it springs from a spark of my splendor. And: I hold up this whole world with one small part of myself. These are his vibhutis, his shinings: places where the divine shows through most clearly. Here's the teaching. Krishna doesn't say the ocean is all of God. He says God shines in the best of each kind, so an ocean, a great river or a mountain can lead the mind to him. That's why a family at the beach may fold their hands to the sea, why the Ganga is bathed in as holy, and why pilgrims walk around Mount Kailasa. Now the letter. A is the plainest sound there is: open the mouth, let the voice out, don't shape it. A. It's where the Sanskrit alphabet begins. And in Devanagari, the script Sanskrit is often written in, a consonant carries a short a inside it unless a mark says otherwise. The letter for k is read ka; for m, ma. So the a runs, quietly, through almost every letter on the page. Many teachers read that as Krishna's point: the divine is the plainest thing, running through everything else. This week, the sounds of the sacred words, and what they carry.
screen: `OCEAN, HIMALAYA, GANGA, THE LETTER A.` · `VIBHUTI: WHERE GOD SHINES THROUGH.` · `THE BEST OF EACH KIND.` · `A HIDES INSIDE EVERY CONSONANT.` · then, large: `THE PLAINEST SOUND RUNS THROUGH ALL.`

segments.voice: Let the jaw soften, breathe in through the nose, and on the out-breath let a quiet, unshaped sound come out: a, like the start of the word about. Let it last as long as the breath, then rest in the silence. If you pray, let each a be a small bow to the one Krishna says runs through it; if not, just notice where the sound seems to come from. If sound isn't possible where you are, say it inwardly.
A. The open mouth, the plainest sound, the letter Krishna names among his shinings, hidden inside almost every letter on the page.
Your line: vibhuti, God shines in the best of everything. Tomorrow: how did a robber become a saint by saying a name backwards? Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindus honor the divine shining in the greatest of each kind, as Krishna lists in Gita 10: bathing in the Ganga, folding hands to the sea, going on pilgrimage to great mountains; students of Sanskrit also learn that the letter a, which Krishna names among letters, sounds inside almost every consonant.

fork.setup: a friend asks: 'if God is in everything, why bow to the ocean in particular?' by Gita 10, what fits?
options: God shines most clearly in the best of each kind, so the ocean leads the mind to him.
the ocean isn't special; God lives only in temples.
the ocean is all of God, and nothing else is.
fork.reveal: among waters, I am the ocean: whatever is glorious springs from a spark of Krishna's splendor. a shining, not the whole.

original.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: a, the first letter, the open mouth. Krishna names it in Gita 10.33.

trapdoor: what you thought: Krishna picked the letter a at random.
what it means: the a runs through almost every letter, the way the divine runs through everything; it's one of his vibhutis.
what a scholar hears: aksharanam akaro 'smi, Gita 10.33, inside the vibhuti list that closes with 10.41–42.

chat.meaning: In Gita 10, Krishna says among waters he is the ocean, and whatever is glorious springs from a spark of his splendor. Nani bows to God shining through the sea.
